summary: Rutland County, VT timber tower in use from 1934; taken down in 1953-54 after decay; no source found describing the site today.

facts.design: Timber tower with watchman's camp; glass-enclosed cab planned for 1933. A 1942 survey note describes a steel structure, which the 1933 newspaper and the 1953-54 state report do not match.
facts.status_note: Tower taken down in 1953-54 per the state biennial report. No source describes what, if anything, remains.
facts.agency: Vermont Department of Conservation (per 1942 survey note)

events.note: Lookout site selected in 1932; timber tower and watchman's camp built that year with local labor (per 1933 newspaper).
New lookout tower in operation by June 1934 (Rutland Daily Herald, 16 June 1934).
James McIntyre named as watchman; first named staffer in the sources.
Watchman reported fires in Castleton, Poultney, Wells and Middleton Springs; all were put out before serious damage.
1940-42 state report: new girders and braces put in the tower.
Harold Hathaway of North Rupert stationed at the tower (Rutland Daily Herald, April 1952).
1953-54 state report: wooden tower dismantled and razed as decayed beyond repair; site lease terminated; telephone line salvaged.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1942 survey note describes a steel structure; the 1933 newspaper (native spruce timbers) and the 1953-54 state report (old wooden tower) describe a wooden tower. The story names both the steel description from 1942 and the wooden descriptions from 1933 and 1953-54, and notes the disagreement.

A June 1934 newspaper places the tower in Poultney; a 1933 newspaper says the mountain is near Middletown Springs, and the 1953-54 state report says Middleton. All are in Rutland County. The story does not pick one town.

notes_for_editor: Thin: two sources, and the state reports are read through the Forest Lookouts transcription, not the originals. The 1942 survey note (steel, glass cage, owned by the state) conflicts with the 1933 newspaper and the 1953-54 state report (both wooden); the story reports both. The town name also varies across sources. No source describes the site today. The 1933 glass-cab entry is future tense in the newspaper, so no event is recorded for it. Access is not set because no source describes it. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 4 page reads. The search snippets were not cited.
